extracted.intended_audience: chemical manufacturers, SDS preparers, importers, downstream manufacturers, employers, and other OSHA/HCS stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements for preparing Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard (HCS), addressing content and formatting requirements for Sections 2, 3, 8, and 9 (and related appendices) including trade secrets, identifiers, exposure limits, and physical/chemical property reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard classification must include intrinsic hazards (paragraph (d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Hazard classification must include hazards associated with the chemical's intrinsic properties including: (i) a change in the chemical's physical form and; (ii) chemical reaction products associated with known or reasonably anticipated uses or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA revised paragraph (d)(1) into two subparagraphs to make clear classification must account for intrinsic hazards such as changes in physical form and reaction products. See also discussion in Summary and Explanation for paragraph (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 2 wording — classify, not just identify, reaction hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2 (c) now begins with: 'Hazards classified under paragraph (d)(1)(ii)...' to clarify manufacturers and importers must classify for reaction hazards rather than merely mention them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA replaced proposed language that only said 'Hazards identified under normal conditions of use...' to align Section 2 with paragraph (d)(1) and remove ambiguity about whether classification is required for reaction hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information about hazardous substances formed during use — Sections 2 and 10 (not necessarily Sections 3/8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For situations where hazardous substances form during use but the substance is not present in its hazardous state in the mixture as shipped, manufacturers are not required to provide this information in Sections 3 or 8 because the resulting hazardous substance is not an ingredient or constituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA expects manufacturers to include information on substances formed by chemical reactions in Sections 2 and 10 (including occupational exposure limits, e.g., PELs/TLVs under Section 10(d) Conditions to Avoid). See OSHA LOI (2016-05-20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream reaction hazards cannot be relegated solely to Section 16
rubrics_metrics.description: Hazards from downstream chemical reactions must be included in Section 2; they may not be addressed solely in Section 16 when the intrinsic properties of the chemical create the hazard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA disagrees with suggestions to put such hazards only in Section 16 (other potential issues) because Section 2 is intended to address intrinsic property hazards; classification is based on intrinsic properties, not anticipated exposure (except where the chemical is bound such that exposure cannot occur—see 2015 LOI). Manufacturers must provide additional toxicity info in Section 11 and may provide additional info in Section 16, but hazard info must appear in Section 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting percent of ingredients of unknown acute toxicity (Section 2(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers are required to state the exact percentage of a mixture that is composed of ingredients of unknown acute toxicity if the concentration of at least one such ingredient is ≥ one percent and the mixture is not classified based on testing of the mixture as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers need not report individual concentrations of ingredients with unknown toxicity in Section 2, but must report the total percentage of unknown toxicity (may include multiple chemicals). They may not use the prescribed ranges in paragraph (i) for reporting unknown acute toxicity. If CBI concerns exist, SDS preparers may still withhold the name of the chemical.

rubrics_metrics.name: List 'additives (constituents)' in Section 3 for substances
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA adds '(constituents)' to paragraph (d) to clarify the term 'additives' so that any individual part of an additive that contributes to classification needs to be listed in Section 3 of the SDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No comments objected; this clarifies that constituents of additives that contribute to classification are to be disclosed in Section 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require chemical name and unique identifier for ingredients in mixtures (Section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3 requires the chemical name of each ingredient in a mixture that is classified as a health hazard and requires inclusion of the CAS number or other unique identifier for these ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA intends CAS numbers be provided when available. Where a CAS number is not available or is CBI-protected, another unique identifier must be provided (e.g., internal product number), and the SDS preparer must include the source of that unique identifier so recipients can use it to identify the chemical in emergency and non-emergency situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-secret disclosure statement and concentration-range requirements (Section 3 / paragraph (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trade secret is claimed in accordance with paragraph (i), 'a statement that the specific chemical identity, and/or concentration (exact or range) of the composition has been withheld as a trade secret is required.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA added 'and/or' to clarify that identity and concentration may both be withheld. When concentration or concentration range is withheld as a trade secret, SDS preparers must use the prescribed concentration ranges in §1910.1200(f)(1)(iv)-(vi) in Section 3 (i.e., report the concentration in accordance with the prescribed ranges). OSHA declined to add 'as appropriate' because the SDS must already state which information is withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing requirement — chemical name and concentration for health-hazard ingredients (Section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HCS requires Section 3 of the SDS to include the chemical name and concentration (exact percentage or ranges) of all ingredients which are classified as 'health hazards' in accordance with paragraph (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA did not change this requirement but sought comments on expanding it to physical hazards and HNOCs; OSHA will consider comments for future updates but did not finalize expansion in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream reliance on upstream supplier information (Section 3/impurities/additives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Downstream manufacturers may continue to rely on information provided by their upstream suppliers regarding impurities and stabilizing additives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA states modifications to paragraph (d) and Appendix D, Table D.1 Section 3 have not altered the ability of downstream manufacturers to rely on upstream supplier information.

rubrics_metrics.name: List occupational exposure limits in Section 8(a) for all Section 3 ingredients regardless of concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 8(a) requires the SDS to include the OSHA PEL, the ACGIH TLV, and any other exposure limit used or recommended by the chemical manufacturer, importer, or employer preparing the SDS, when available, for all ingredients or constituents listed in Section 3 regardless of the concentration at which they are present in a mixture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ingredient has no OSHA PEL, ACGIH TLV, or other exposure limit used or recommended by the preparer, it does not need to be listed in Section 8. OSHA views this clarification as not changing existing requirements but clarifying applicability to all Section 3 ingredients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a range of exposure limits in Section 8 when a range is used/recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: SDS preparers must include a range of exposure limits in Section 8 whenever a range is used or recommended by the chemical manufacturer, importer, or employer preparing the SDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement responds to tools like occupational exposure banding. OSHA will not mandate inclusion of supporting documentation or hyperlinks on how the range was established due to practicality concerns; preparers may provide supporting info in Section 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of additional OELs (NIOSH RELs, state limits) — not mandated in this rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Although commenters asked to add NIOSH RELs or state-specific limits, OSHA did not add these as mandatory requirements in this final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8(a) may include any exposure limit or range used or recommended by the SDS preparer where available, but requiring RELs/state limits would be a substantive change and was outside the scope of this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPE specification in Section 8(c) — no change (generic statements still allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA did not propose changes to Section 8(c) and has not required manufacturers to list specific types of required PPE based on 'actual hazard' or to prohibit generic statements such as 'use appropriate glove' or 'use appropriate NIOSH Approved Respirator'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments requesting more prescriptive PPE language were considered out of scope for this rulemaking and are discussed elsewhere; Appendix C discussion addresses label PPE language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align Section 9 physical/chemical properties text with GHS Rev.7 (in HCS text only)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA proposed to list the required physical and chemical properties of the chemical in the same order that appears in Annex 4 of the GHS Rev.7 in the HCS text (not requiring SDS preparers to order properties on the SDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alignment is meant to simplify global preparation of SDSs; OSHA clarifies the order requirement applies to the HCS text, not the SDS document itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 9 property wording changes and parenthetical clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace 'appearance' with 'physical state' and 'color'; eliminate 'odor threshold' and 'evaporation rate' as separate required properties but retain odor threshold under 'Odor' (add parenthetical 'includes odor threshold') and retain evaporation rate under 'Vapor pressure' (add parenthetical 'includes evaporation rate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA is adding parentheticals to prevent confusion and ensure odor threshold and evaporation rate information remain available if appropriate. OSHA declined to require statements about olfactory fatigue because that does not align with Rev.7 and Section 9 limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify 'kinematic viscosity' as the viscosity parameter in Section 9
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA is adding the term 'kinematic' to the property 'viscosity' to better define the appropriate parameter to be characterized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that kinematic—not dynamic—viscosity is the intended measurement for SDS reporting under Section 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add 'particle characteristics' as a required property for solids in Section 9
rubrics_metrics.description: Add 'particle characteristics' as a new physical property for solids; particle characteristics should include the particle size (median and range) and, if available and appropriate, further properties such as size distribution (range), shape, aspect ratio, and specific surface area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIOSH recommended inclusion of particle size distribution and other standardized particle metrics; NIOSH also suggested surface reactivity and density as important determinants of toxicity for inhaled particles, especially for nanomaterials. OSHA acknowledges significance for engineered nanomaterials and included particle characteristics to improve hazard communication.
